title: Dual antibody strategy for high-resolution imaging of murine Purkinje cells and their dendrites across multiple layers
protocol: Prepare milliQ water.
Prepare PBS 1× solution.
Unfreeze 4% PFA at room temperature if previously stored at -20°C.
Fill Scintillation vials with 10 mL of 4% PFA in PBS 1× solution.
Prepare surgical instruments needed for brain extraction: scissors, forceps, spatula.
Fill the tubing with PBS 1× by inserting the free end into a falcon tube containing PBS 1× solution and turning on the peristaltic pump until solution starts coming from the needle on the other end.
Anesthetize the mouse by injecting Avertin or an IACUC-approved alternative such as a Ketamine cocktail.
Pinch the animal's foot with surgical tweezers after 10 minutes to check for full anesthesia.
Place the fully anesthetized animal on its back on a raised flat surface such as a plastic tray or styrofoam.
Fix the paws in place using tape or needles if using styrofoam.
Make an incision on the abdomen with standard dissecting scissors, being careful not to damage the liver.
Cut through the diaphragm and along the rib cage gently to reveal the heart, avoiding contact with the liver.
Lift the upper part of the rib cage by cutting between the ribs toward the spinal cord while avoiding the lungs.
Insert a 27G needle into the left ventricle shallowly to avoid damaging the heart.
Turn on the pump at 36 mL/min from the PBS 1× falcon tube.
Make a small incision on the right atrium and observe thick blood flow.
Continue perfusing with PBS 1× until the liver changes color from dark to light brown.
Perfuse until body structures, such as paws, become white.
Cut the end of the tail and wait for clear drops of PBS 1× to appear, indicating complete perfusion.
Transfer the free end of tubing into the falcon containing 50 mL of 4% PFA (usually 25 mL are enough) when PBS clears.
Resume pumping until PFA solution enters the system; observe twitching in tail and paws.
Stop pump when paws and tail become rigid and inflexible.
Remove needle from heart, flush with water, refill tubes and needles with 1× PBS for next animal.
Decapitate mouse at neck using bandage scissors, removing skin longitudinally from neck to ears.
Use Iris scissors to remove skull longitudinally from occipital region to nasal bones.
Lift right and left portions of skull bone with forceps to reveal brain.
Remove brain using spatula and place in 20 mL vial containing 10 mL of 4% PFA.
Keep brain overnight in 4% PFA solution at 4°C.
Replace brain tissue in the vial with 5% sucrose in PBS 1×, gently shake for 1 h at 4°C.
Replace the sucrose 5% solution with 10% sucrose water solution, gently shake for 1 h at 4°C.
Replace with 20% sucrose water solution and wait until the brain sinks to the bottom of the vial.
When the brain has sunk to the bottom of the vial again, replace with 30% sucrose water solution and place the vial at 4°C overnight.
Remove the brain from 30% sucrose solution with a spatula.
Place the brain on a Kimwipe and dry it by applying extremely light pressure.
Remove extra sucrose between the brain hemispheres using a small 10 μL tip.
Delicately push the Kimwipe between the brain hemispheres to remove excess sucrose.
Place the brain into a freezing mold.
Cover the brain with Tissue-Plus™ O.C.T. Compound at room temperature slowly to avoid bubbles.
Flip over the brain in the compound several times to coat it uniformly.
Gently transfer the coated brain to the bottom of a new freezing mold.
Push the brain down gently to make it as flat as possible.
Prepare sagittal sections of the brain.
Place the brain flat at the bottom of a freezing mold.
Annotate the front, rear, left, and right sides of the brain outside the mold with a permanent marker.
Alternatively, cut the brain in half along the sagittal axis before embedding.
Surround the freezing mold containing the brain and O.C.T. with dry ice to solidify the O.C.T. slowly.
Remove the frozen O.C.T.-embedded brain from the mold.
Fix the frontal-occipital part of the brain into a cryostat chuck using a small amount of O.C.T. in dry ice.
Mount the frozen O.C.T.-embedded tissue on a Leica CM3050S Cryostat.
Start sectioning the sagittally oriented brain at 40 μm thickness.
Place O.C.T.-embedded tissues at -20°C in the cryostat for two hours to equilibrate the tissue before sectioning.
Collect slices in a 12-well plate filled with 1 mL of PBS 1× with 0.02% Sodium Azide.
Store collected slices at 4°C.
Mount brain slices starting from the middle sections of the brain in 12-well plates.
Transfer brain slices to new 12-well plates filled with PBS using a modified transfer pipet.
Rinse slices in PBS for 10 minutes on a Rocker II at room temperature.
Remove PBS from the wells using a transfer pipette.
Block sections with 0.5 mL-1 mL of blocking solution.
Gently shake the sections for 1 hour at 4°C on a Rocker II.
Select sections from the middle of the brain to cover the entire cerebellum structure.
Incubate the sections in 0.5 mL blocking solution containing primary antibodies for 48 h at 4°C, gently shaking.
Wash the sections 4 times with TBS-T for 20 min each, gently shaking.
Wrap the 12-well plate with aluminum foil to avoid bleaching of fluorescent signals.
Incubate the sections in 0.5 mL blocking solution containing secondary antibody conjugated to a fluorophore at 4°C for 48 h, gently shaking.
Wash the sections 4 times with TBS-T for 20 min each, gently shaking.
Rinse off TBS-T with PBS before mounting the sections.
Treat plastic transfer pipette with 2% BSA in PBS.
Transfer sections to a PIREX reusable Petri dish filled halfway with PBS using treated transfer pipette.
Gently arrange the sections to the slides using the brush without folds or wrinkles.
Remove the extra PBS 1× with vacuum or Kimwipe.
Use one drop of PROLONG-GOLD antifade mounting medium for one 25 mm × 25 mm cover glass.
Remove excess mounting medium around the cover glass and between the slide and cover glass with a vacuum using a 200 μL tip.
Leave the slides in the dark and let them dry overnight.
Seal the slides the following day with clear nail polish.
Let the sealed slides dry and store at 4°C.
Acquire images of cerebella stained with IP3R1 and Calbindin at 20× magnification using the Z-Stack imaging function.
Acquire images of cerebella stained with IP3R1 and Calbindin at 63× magnification using the Z-Stack imaging function.
Make a 3D-reconstruction of the Z-Stack acquired using Leica Application Suite Advanced Fluorescence pre-standard and automatic “Volume reconstruction” function.
Save all the images in single channel format.
Save all the 3D reconstructed images.
